title: Multiple Parameters
story: You're building a recipe app. A smoothie function needs both fruit AND liquid — one ingredient alone won't blend!
why: Real-world functions rarely need just one input. Multiple parameters let you pass all the data a function needs in a single call.
analogy: Function parameters are like labeled slots in a vending machine — you must put the right thing in the right slot.
try_it: Write a function with four parameters that builds a full address: street, city, state, and zip code. Call it with your own address (real or made up).
tips: Arguments match parameters by position — first to first, second to second
Use descriptive parameter names so callers know what goes where
Each parameter needs its own type annotation: `(x: Int, y: Str)` not `(x, y: Str)`
common_mistakes: Swapping argument order accidentally — `subtract(3, 10)` gives -7, not 7
Passing the wrong type — `add("5", 3)` when the function expects `Int, Int`
Forgetting to type each parameter individually — only the last one gets the annotation
